findings.evidence: Table 3-3, printed p. 57: "the challenger's own 32L/4096H GQA (8 KV-heads × 128) = 0.131 MB/token at FP16 × 9,200 ≈ 1.20 GB". Earlier in §3.3.3, printed p. 45: "so 9,200 × 0.0655 MB ≈ 0.60 GB (≈1.2 GB at FP16)".
findings.issue: The FP16 KV for the 32L/4096H GQA challenger is stated as ~1.20 GB in Table 3-3 but as ~1.2 GB in §3.3.3. The exact value from the table's own inputs is 9,200 × 131,072 B = 1,205,862,400 B = 1.2059 GB, which rounds to 1.21 GB, not 1.20 GB. Table 3-3's "≈ 1.20 GB" is a truncation; the prose's "≈1.2 GB" is a coarse rounding. Neither is the rounded value 1.21 GB. The 8-bit row has the same issue: 9,200 × 65,536 B = 602,931,200 B = 0.6029 GB, which the table prints as "≈ 0.60 GB" — also a truncation, not a rounding.
findings.fix_instruction: In Table 3-3 and in §3.3.3, print the FP16 challenger KV as ~1.21 GB (1,205,862,400 B) and the 8-bit challenger KV as ~0.603 GB (602,931,200 B), or state explicitly that the 1.20 / 0.60 figures are truncations of the exact byte counts. Do not mix truncated table values with rounded prose values for the same quantity.

findings.evidence: "Compute ratio vs dense 70B | ~0.183× (≈18% of dense 70B compute) | (12.8B × 2) ÷ (70B × 2) = 25.6 GFLOP ÷ 140 GFLOP ≈ 0.183×"
findings.issue: 12.8B × 2 = 25.6 GFLOP. 70B × 2 = 140 GFLOP. 25.6/140 = 0.18286 ≈ 0.183. Correct. The text then says 'the canonical 70B dense baseline costs about 5.5× the compute per token'. 1/0.183 = 5.46 ≈ 5.5. Correct. Arithmetic verified — no defect.

findings.evidence: "~47B MoE challenger (Mixtral 8x7B class): KV per token = 2 × 32 × 8 × 128 = 65,536 B = 0.0655 MB/token at 8-bit, so 9,200 × 0.0655 MB ≈ 0.60 GB (≈1.2 GB at FP16)"
findings.issue: 2 × 32 × 8 × 128 = 65,536 B. This is correct for the GQA KV per token at 1 byte (8-bit). 65,536 B = 0.065536 MB ≈ 0.0655 MB. Correct. 9,200 × 0.065536 MB = 602.9 MB ≈ 0.60 GB. Correct. At FP16 (2 bytes): 65,536 × 2 = 131,072 B per token. 9,200 × 131,072 = 1,205,862,400 B ≈ 1.21 GB ≈ 1.2 GB. Correct. Arithmetic verified — no defect.
